svg.title: Choose the Buyer Before the File Format
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-buyer-to-supported-product; chapter number: 1; title: Choose the Buyer Before the File Format; subtitle: Research the problem, create a useful product, connect the offer, and make delivery understandable.; caption: Victor Jaro emphasizes buyer research; Baddie In Business demonstrates Canva production; Rochelle Be connects a free win to a paid offer; Richard Yu simplifies sales links; Tatyana Savage supplies access instructions.; assumptions note: These practitioners describe complementary practices, not a jointly operated business or a guaranteed sales sequence.; note: Jaro reports no sales from their first student-and-teacher templates. Savage describes instructions in listing images and delivered files as a way to reduce customer questions.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Research the buyer; value: Step 1; detail: Victor Jaro researches the buyer and topic before investing hours in a paid Notion template.; step: 02; label: Build the useful product; value: Step 2; detail: Baddie In Business duplicates a working Canva page layout and exports the ebook as PDF standard.; step: 03; label: Connect a small win; value: Step 3; detail: Rochelle Be makes the freebie goal-specific and outcome-focused, with a direct connection to the paid product.; step: 04; label: Simplify the purchase path; value: Step 4; detail: Richard Yu links a single product directly to its sales page and recommends at most three intermediate links when several offers are available.; step: 05; label: Explain access and usage; value: Step 5; detail: Tatyana Savage puts download instructions and FAQs in listing images and usage instructions inside the delivered files.
